ig_caption:
A one-line rename just deleted a database. Terraform said: Apply complete! 💥

AI refactored this Terraform and renamed a resource "for clarity":
docker_container.db → docker_container.orders_db

Terraform doesn't see a rename. It sees one resource gone and a new one:
⚠️ plan: 1 to add, 1 to destroy
⚠️ apply: the orders table is gone

The fix:
✅ a moved block (from = old address, to = new address)
✅ read every plan; destroy on a database is a stop sign

Same rename → 0 destroyed → all 3 orders still there.

Save this before your next refactor 🔖 and follow for more fixes like this.

#terraform #devops #iac #infrastructureascode #ai
yt_title: Terraform rename deleted the database. AI wrote it #terraform
yt_description:
Real run (Terraform 1.14 + Docker provider, local Postgres container, demo data):
- renaming a resource address makes Terraform plan destroy + create; apply wipes the data
- fix: a moved block from the old address to the new one, so the plan shows "has moved" and 0 to destroy, and all rows survive
- for real databases, also consider lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }
